## Why This Is Asked
Tests multi-cloud, per-tenant isolation, and scalable state management across clouds.

- Provider aliases and per-tenant configuration

- Cross-cloud connectivity testing and drift detection

```javascript

variable "tenants" {
  type = map(object{
    aws_alias  string
    aws_region string
    gcp_alias  string
    gcp_region string
``` 

## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to scale environments with for_each while reusing a wrapper module, plus enforce governance via a CI gate.

## Key Concepts
- Terraform for_each over a map to create multiple subnets
- Local validations to ensure CIDR uniqueness
- Reusing a shared module with environment tagging
- CI gate with GitHub Actions that blocks prod-touching changes

## Code Example
```javascript
variable "team_subnets" {
  type = map(string)
  default = {
    Alpha = "10.0.1.0/24",
    Beta  = "10.0.2.0/24",
    Gamma = "10.0.3.0/24"
  }
}
locals {
  cidrs = [for _, cidr in var.team_subnets : cidr]
}
validation "cidr_uniqueness" {
  condition = length(distinct(local.cidrs)) == length(local.cidrs)
  error_message = "Subnets CIDRs must be unique"
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you detect overlapping CIDRs beyond simple duplicates?
- How would you extend the gate to also verify minimum tag coverage on new resources?

## Why This Is Asked

- Terraform plan JSON workflow
- OPA/rego policy for infrastructure gating

```hcl

  id = var.aws_shared_sg_id
}
```

```rego
package terraform.gate

deny[msg] {
  input.resource_changes[_] = rc
  rc.change.actions[_] = "create"
  some ingress_rule
  ingress_rule := rc.change.after.ingress[_]
  ingress_rule.ip_ranges[_] = "0.0.0.0/0"
  msg = "Opening 0.0.0.0/0 ingress is not allowed"
}
```

```hcl
# wrappers/main.tf
variable "environment" { type = string }

module "env" {
  source = "./modules/env"
  environment = var.environment
}
```

```hcl
# modules/env/providers.tf
variable "environment" { type = string }

provider "google" {
  alias   = "gcp"
  project = var.environment == "prod" ? "prod-project" : "dev-project"
  region  = "us-central1"
}

provider "oci" {
  alias      = "oci"
  tenancy_id = var.environment == "prod" ? var.tenancy_prod : var.tenancy_dev
  region     = var.environment == "prod" ? "us-ashburn-1" : "us-ashburn-1"
}
```

## Why This Is Asked

- Cross-module outputs/inputs wiring

```hcl
# wrapper module: modules/env_logs/main.tf
variable "env_map" {
  type = map(object({ enabled = bool; bucket_suffix = string }))
}

resource "aws_s3_bucket" "log_buckets" {
  for_each = { for k, v in var.env_map : k => v if v.enabled }
  bucket   = "vpc-logs-${each.key}-${each.value.bucket_suffix}"
  acl      = "private"
}

output "log_buckets" {
  value = [for b in aws_s3_bucket.log_buckets : b.id]
}
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical understanding of per-environment state management, modular composition, and CI governance in Terraform without complex infrastructure. Demonstrates concrete architectural patterns and how wrapper modules propagate environment context across resources.

## Key Concepts
- Per-environment remote state using a single backend with environment-specific keys
- Wrapper module pattern to inject environment context and enforce consistent tagging
- CI gate that whitelists allowed plan changes to prevent drift into production
- Simple, beginner-friendly approach that scales to additional environments

## Code Example
```hcl
# modules/env_wrapper/main.tf
variable "environment" {
  description = "Environment name"
  type        = string
}

variable "instance_config" {
  description = "EC2 instance configuration"
  type        = object({
    ami           = string
    instance_type = string
  })
}

locals {
  common_tags = {
    Environment = var.environment
    ManagedBy   = "terraform"
  }
}

resource "aws_instance" "main" {
  ami           = var.instance_config.ami
  instance_type = var.instance_config.instance_type
  
  tags = merge(local.common_tags, {
    Name = "${var.environment}-ec2-instance"
  })
}
```

```hcl
# environments/dev/backend.tf
terraform {
  backend "s3" {
    bucket         = "my-terraform-state"
    key            = "terraform/state/dev/env.tfstate"
    region         = "us-east-1"
    encrypt        = true
    dynamodb_table = "terraform-locks"
  }
}
```

```hcl
# environments/prod/backend.tf
terraform {
  backend "s3" {
    bucket         = "my-terraform-state"
    key            = "terraform/state/prod/env.tfstate"
    region         = "us-east-1"
    encrypt        = true
    dynamodb_table = "terraform-locks"
  }
}
```

```yaml
# .github/workflows/terraform-plan.yml
name: Terraform Plan
on:
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]

jobs:
  terraform-plan:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    strategy:
      matrix:
        environment: [dev, staging, prod]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - uses: hashicorp/setup-terraform@v2
        
      - name: Terraform Plan
        run: |
          cd environments/${{ matrix.environment }}
          terraform init
          terraform plan -out=plan.tfplan
          
      - name: Validate Plan Changes
        run: |
          cd environments/${{ matrix.environment }}
          terraform show -json plan.tfplan > plan.json
          
          # Check for non-whitelisted changes in non-prod
          if [ "${{ matrix.environment }}" != "prod" ]; then
            # Only allow tag updates in non-prod environments
            if jq -e '.resource_changes[] | select(.change.actions[] != "no-op" and (.change.before.tags == null or .change.after.tags == null))' plan.json; then
              echo "Error: Non-tag changes detected in ${{ matrix.environment }} environment"
              exit 1
            fi
          fi
```

## Why This Is Asked

- Terraform plan JSON parsing
- CI gates in GitHub Actions

## Code Example

```python
# gate.py
import json, sys
plan = json.load(open(sys.argv[1]))
for rc in plan.get("resource_changes", []):
  actions = rc.get("change", {}).get("actions", [])
  if any(a in ("create", "update", "delete") for a in actions):
    addr = rc.get("address", "")
    after = rc.get("change", {}).get("after", {})
    tags = after.get("tags", {})
    if addr.startswith("prod") and tags.get("Environment") != "prod":
      print(f"Prod resource missing Environment=prod: {addr}")
      sys.exit(1)
    if not addr.startswith("env-"):
      print(f"Naming violation: {addr}")
      sys.exit(1)
print("Gate passed")
```

- How would you integrate this with Terraform Cloud runs?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to design policy-as-code gates for complex Terraform architectures, ensuring production IAM protections while enabling safe non-prod changes. It also probes how to model environments, source data, and integrate policy evaluation in CI.

- Environment-aware data sources and per-env overrides

## Code Example
```rego
package terraform.authz

default allow = false

deny[msg] {
  plan := input.plan
  env  := input.env
  plan.resource_changes[_].type == "aws_iam_role"
  diff := plan.resource_changes[_].change
  diff.actions[_] == "update"
  diff.after.trust != diff.before.trust
  env == "prod"
  msg = "prod IAM role trust policy changes are not allowed"
}
```
